CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 13, audited at commit 2fb6062 (committed, HEAD of the main
checkout, so the recorded tree hash is the audited content). Sprint file re-read fresh
immediately before this verdict. Six files, 1516 insertions.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. Two required fixes, both small, both against acceptance
criteria the sprint file names explicitly. Everything else is met, and the hard parts
are met well.

REQUIRED FIX 1 -- the body mark colours are not the handoff's.

The handoff specifies three body colours (docs/design/HANDOFF_chart_constellation.md,
the Body marks paragraph):

  luminaries         oklch(0.88 0.06 85)
  direct planets     oklch(0.80 0.05 145)
  retrograde planets oklch(0.74 0.11 25)

app/chart/constellation.ts instead reuses the aspect thread palette for body marks:
COLOR_GOLD oklch(0.84 0.07 85), COLOR_VERDIGRIS oklch(0.70 0.13 145), COLOR_RUST
oklch(0.68 0.13 25). I grepped the whole of app/ for the three handoff values: none of
them appear anywhere in the codebase. This is not a near-miss on one channel, it is
three different colours.

The direct-planet case is the visible one: 0.70 lightness / 0.13 chroma against a
specified 0.80 / 0.05 is a markedly darker, markedly more saturated green -- eight of
the ten marks, most of the time. The handoff's Fidelity section says colours are final
and should be matched closely, the sprint file makes the handoff the acceptance
reference, and its acceptance criterion says "colours ... match the handoff".

What makes this a fix rather than a note: this project records its deliberate
deviations. R7 departs from the handoff's client-generated UUID and the sprint file
says so, with reasoning. This departure is recorded nowhere, which means it reads as
exactly the thing the sprint's own risk register calls "fidelity drift under time
pressure ... their absence is what makes a build look like a facsimile". Either use the
handoff's values, or record the deviation the way R7's is recorded. Note that
constellation.test.ts:49 asserts the current values, so the test locks the deviation in
rather than catching it -- that test needs updating with the fix.

REQUIRED FIX 2 -- the orb table is redeclared in app/.

  app/chart/constellation.ts:85  export const ASPECT_MAX_ORB = {
    conjunction: 8, opposition: 8, trine: 7, square: 7, sextile: 4 }

The acceptance criterion is explicit: "Aspect orbs in particular must match Sprint
12's, not be redeclared here." I grepped for every use of ASPECT_MAX_ORB across the
repo: there are none. It is exported and entirely unreferenced -- dead code. The
values do match Sprint 12's, so nothing is wrong today, and the rendering correctly
consumes Sprint 12's `tightness` field (constellation.ts:206 passes a.tightness
through; page.tsx:275-276 derives width and opacity from it) rather than recomputing
1 - orb/maxOrb locally. Which is the right design, and is why the constant is unused.
Delete the five lines. A dead orb table in the UI layer is a second home for a number
that has one home, and the next person who needs maxOrb will reach for the near one.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET. Both states built. Geometry checked value by value against the handoff:
  centre 320,320; radius 78 + ring*22 with ring order Moon 0 through Pluto 9, so radii
  run 78-276; screen angle (180 - lon); dot radius 3.6 luminaries / 2.6 otherwise;
  glyph at r-15, label at r+16, text-anchor end on the left half; sector spokes r=60
  to r=288 at each 30 degree boundary with the sign glyph at r=306; sign glyph fill
  oklch(0.72 0.09 145) when occupied, oklch(0.34 0.02 288) otherwise. Star field: 110
  stars, seed 20260816, radius band 40-308, r 0.4-1.6, opacity 0.12-0.52, twinkle
  5-14s, delay 0-6s -- every one of those matches. Thread weight
  baseWidth * (0.5 + tight) and opacity 0.22 + tight * 0.5, hover 2.2x and 0.95,
  isolated 0.07: all as specified. Moon phase path reproduces the handoff's arc
  formula exactly, including cy=354. Animation timings: drift 12s, turn 260s, halo 8s,
  breathe and twinkle var-driven -- all as specified. This is careful work; the
  colours in fix 1 are the exception, not the pattern.
R2 MET, and this was the criterion I checked hardest. Grepped app/ for Keplerian
  element tables, mean anomaly, eccentricity, obliquity, perihelion, AU, and the
  distinctive numeric constants from the prototype's own ephemeris: zero hits. Every
  import in app/chart traces to lib/ephemeris/ -- adapter, aspects, balance,
  julian-day, moon-phase, zodiac. constellation.ts imports PlanetPosition and Aspect
  as types and computes nothing but screen coordinates. The most copyable thing in the
  bundle was not copied.
R3 MET. No browser chrome bar anywhere in the diff.
R4 MET, and verified empirically rather than by reading the import. next/font/google
  for Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex Mono, no <link> and no @import anywhere. Then
  the real check: built the app and grepped the entire .next output for
  fonts.googleapis, fonts.gstatic and googleapis.com -- zero hits, with 25 self-hosted
  .woff2 assets under .next/static/media. Then served it and grepped the delivered
  HTML for any absolute URL: none. The zero-outbound-calls property survives.
R5 MET. The range input's onChange fires on every input event in React, and it is
  wrapped in startTransition -- which is the sprint's own stated allowance. The
  recompute is a useMemo keyed on [baseDate, time, offset], so positions, aspects,
  counts and phase all move together when the scrub moves.
R6 MET. Five ambient animations exist and the prefers-reduced-motion block disables
  all five (.ornament for drift, .ornamentStars for turn, .animBreathe, .animTwinkle,
  .animHalo). Nothing legibility-carrying is animated, so the static chart stands.
R7 MET. randomUUID stays in app/chart/actions.ts under "use server". No client-side id
  generation anywhere. The comment records the deviation from the handoff and why,
  which is the pattern fix 1 is missing.
R8 MET. Loading: the seal button becomes "Sealing..." and disables while saving.
  Errors: computed-state failures and save failures both render through
  styles.errorText in a role="alert" paragraph, using existing tokens, unelaborated.
  Sprint 10's R7 still binds and still holds -- the action returns an error state
  instead of redirecting, and no success state is shown for a write that did not
  complete.
R9 MET. README states the desktop-only >=1320px constraint and frames it as future
  work rather than a bug.
R10 MET. Time UT input present, feeding instantFromDateAndTime.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 119 tests across 12 files, 9 new and all with
  real assertions -- star field determinism and count, the 180-lon angle mapping,
  label formatting, sector occupancy, and two moon-phase geometry cases.
- next build exits 0. Route table: /_not-found, /api/health/db, /chart (now static,
  correctly, since it is a client component with local state rather than
  searchParams), /reading/[id].
- Served the built app: / still returns 307 to /chart, so Sprint 11's redirect
  survived the rewrite; /chart serves the empty state with its date input; no external
  host appears in the delivered HTML.
- Sprint 10's guardrails still green in the suite, so the no-listing rule survived a
  full UI replacement -- which the sprint file correctly named as the thing a redesign
  is most likely to break.

Notes, not conditions:
1. Sprint 12's note 1 is now live and user-visible. page.tsx:172 computes the
   lookahead as instant + ONE_DAY_MS and page.tsx:459 renders the result as
   "{aspect} · A/S". My Sprint 12 audit measured this: across 4,588 aspect instances
   over 2024, a one-day lookahead disagrees with a one-hour one on 392 Moon aspects
   and 104 others -- roughly one verdict in nine, and the one-hour answer is the
   correct one, since applying means the orb is closing now. The prototype does the
   same thing (lonAt(jd + 1)), so this is faithful rather than a defect, and I am not
   holding the sprint for it. But it is now printed next to every aspect on the page,
   and the fix is one constant at page.tsx:172 -- computeAspects takes the later
   positions as an argument precisely so the caller can choose. A shorter step for the
   aspect call, keeping a day for retrograde detection, costs one extra
   computePositions per render. Somebody who owns the design should decide, now that
   it is visible rather than theoretical.
2. The Supabase error object in saveReading is still discarded rather than logged --
   carried from Sprint 10 unchanged, still a one-line fix, still means an incident
   would leave no record of why saves are failing.
3. Interactivity is unverified and I want to be precise about what that means rather
   than repeat Dev Team's caveat. I read the interaction code and it is coherent: the
   scrub is wired to a memo that all derived values depend on; hover sets an index
   that the thread opacity and row background both read; the save flow's states are
   both rendered. What I cannot do from a diff is confirm that any of it behaves
   correctly in a browser -- that hover isolation actually isolates, that the redraw
   is fast enough to feel live, that the save round trip works through the new
   component. That is GroundTruth's, and GroundTruth's criteria already cover it,
   including the anonymous-link round trip which is the one that matters most.
4. constellation.test.ts:49 asserts the body colours as currently written. Update it
   alongside fix 1, or the test will hold the deviation in place.

Re-audit after both fixes. Fix 1 is three constants plus one test; fix 2 is deleting
five lines. Keep the re-audit proportionate to that -- nothing else in this diff needs
to move.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 13, round 2. Audited at commit 9b132e3, HEAD of the main checkout,
recorded tree 9f05b82b... Sprint file re-read fresh; its acceptance criteria are
unchanged from round 1. Scope: two files, 15 insertions, 12 deletions.

VERDICT: PASS.

REQUIRED FIX 1 -- body-mark colours. FIXED, exactly.
BODY_COLOR_LUMINARY / BODY_COLOR_DIRECT / BODY_COLOR_RETROGRADE now carry the
handoff's own values -- oklch(0.88 0.06 85), oklch(0.80 0.05 145), oklch(0.74 0.11 25)
-- and computeBodies reads them. I grepped for all three: each now appears in both
constellation.ts and constellation.test.ts, where before none of them existed anywhere
in the repository. The aspect-thread palette is untouched and still feeds
ASPECT_COLOR, which is right: the two palettes are genuinely distinct and only look
like duplication.

Two things lift this above a minimal fix. The comment above the new constants says the
body palette is "close but not identical" to the thread palette and is worth keeping
separate -- which is the note that stops someone deduplicating them back next quarter,
and that recurrence is the actual risk here, not the original slip. And the test now
asserts the handoff's values rather than the code's, so it catches drift instead of
holding it in place. That was the specific thing I asked for and it is the difference
between a test that documents a bug and one that prevents it.

The commit message also gets the classification right: "Not a deliberate deviation
worth recording like R7's -- just drift, now corrected." That distinction is the whole
reason this was a condition rather than a note.

REQUIRED FIX 2 -- redeclared orb table. FIXED. ASPECT_MAX_ORB is deleted, and a grep
across the entire repository returns no references to it. page.tsx continues to read
tightness off the Aspect objects Sprint 12 computes, so there is now exactly one place
in this codebase where an orb maximum is written down, which is the point.

Round 1's coverage stands unchanged -- R1 through R10 all met, verified there against
the handoff value by value, with R2 (no ephemeris in app/) and R4 (no external font
host anywhere in the build or the delivered HTML) checked as the two criteria the
sprint named as mattering most.

Re-verified at 9b132e3:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 119 tests across 12 files, unchanged in count,
  with the three colour assertions now pointing at the handoff.
- next build exits 0; route table unchanged.
- R4 re-probed since the build was regenerated: no fonts.googleapis or fonts.gstatic
  anywhere in .next.

Notes, not conditions. All four carry forward from round 1, and this is the final
sprint of the exercise, so none of them has a later sprint to land in. That is worth
stating plainly rather than leaving "follow-up" to mean nobody:

1. The applying/separating lookahead is now printed next to every aspect on the page
   (page.tsx:172 computes instant + ONE_DAY_MS; page.tsx:459 renders "{aspect} · A/S").
   My Sprint 12 measurement: over 4,588 aspect instances across 2024, a one-day
   lookahead disagrees with a one-hour one on 392 Moon aspects and 104 others, about
   one verdict in nine, and the one-hour answer is the correct one because applying
   means the orb is closing now. The prototype does the same thing, so this is
   faithful to the design rather than a defect, and it is not mine to overrule -- I am
   passing it, as I did in Sprint 12. But it is a design decision that is now visible
   on the product, the fix is one constant at page.tsx:172 plus one extra
   computePositions per render, and there is no Sprint 14 in which to notice it. If
   the answer is "the design says a day and that stands", that is a fine answer;
   it should just be an answer rather than an omission.
2. saveReading still discards the Supabase error object rather than logging it.
   Carried unchanged since Sprint 10. One line, and it is the difference between an
   incident you can diagnose and one you cannot.
3. Interactivity remains unverified by me, and precisely so: I have read the
   interaction code and it is coherent -- the scrub feeds a memo every derived value
   depends on, hover sets an index both the thread opacity and the row background
   read, both save states render. What no diff can tell anyone is whether hover
   isolation actually isolates, whether the live redraw feels live, or whether the
   save round trip survives the new component. GroundTruth's criteria cover all
   three, and its third -- sealing a reading and opening the link in a fresh session
   with no cookies -- is the one that matters most, because it is Sprint 10's
   guarantee surviving a full UI replacement.
4. The static gate has now done everything it can for this epic. Sprints 12 and 13
   between them put an aspect engine and a visualisation into production where the
   only remaining check on the numbers is a person looking at a picture. Sprint 12's
   reference charts and this sprint's geometry tests are what stand between that and
   confident wrong output; they are good, and they are not a substitute for
   GroundTruth confirming a known historical date still matches a published source,
   which its fourth criterion requires.

Cleared to ship at 9b132e3. Standing note for Pipeman: files under docs/sprints/ are
tracked and the tree is dirty with sprint bookkeeping -- do not fold any of it into
the shipped commit, the tree content is what /sprint-ship compares against this
verdict.

CONDITIONAL: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 13, commit
9b132e3abcd7ad8bb4e4b9407daaf05dac69b2af.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-16 ~21:25Z.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. Not because anything is broken -- I found no defect -- but
because this sprint moved the product's primary surface behind JavaScript, and
this session has no browser. Three of the four criteria, including the sprint's
actual proof, cannot be observed with the tools I have. I will not record a PASS
on criteria I did not witness.

THE BLOCKER, ESTABLISHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED
  /chart now renders the empty state server-side and nothing else. The results
  state is produced entirely in the client.
  - GET /chart?date=2024-03-20 returns the EMPTY state, not results. The served
    markup carries <input id="empty-date" ... value=""> and the same empty-state
    copy as the bare /chart.
  - The date is no longer a server-read query parameter. I probed date=, d=,
    when=, moment=, and date=...&sealed=1 -- every one returned the empty-state
    marker "Compute the sky".
  - The submit control ships disabled: <button class="...submit" type="submit"
    disabled=""> . It is enabled by client JS once a date is entered.
  - The form has no action attribute and the page carries no $ACTION_ID, unlike
    Sprint 10's save form which I could drive over plain HTTP.
  - The client chunks reference useSearchParams, so the date is likely reflected
    into the URL client-side after entry, but the server does not read it back.
  Conclusion: without executing JavaScript there is no path to the results state.
  This is a property of the new design, not a fault.

CRITERION 1 -- /chart serves the empty state, and a date produces the results
state with constellation, aspect table, and balance bars. HALF VERIFIED.
  VERIFIED: the empty state serves. HTTP 200, one <svg> present, one date input,
  and the copy renders server-side, verbatim: "The sky keeps its old positions |
  Name a moment that has already passed. The planets will be put back where they
  stood. | Date past | Compute the sky | No account. No place of birth. No houses.
  | Nothing kept but what you choose to seal."
  NOT VERIFIED: the results state. I never reached it. Constellation, aspect
  table, and balance bars are entirely unobserved.

CRITERION 2 -- scrubbing changes the figure live; positions, aspects and counts
all move. NOT TESTED.
  Scrubbing is an input-event-driven client recompute (R5 requires redraw on every
  input event). It has no HTTP surface at all. There is nothing for curl to do
  here -- this is not a case where I found a workaround and it failed, it is a
  case where no non-browser observation exists.

CRITERION 3 -- sealing returns a link, and opening it in a fresh session with no
cookies renders the saved reading. HALF VERIFIED, and the unverified half is the
sprint's actual proof.
  NOT VERIFIED -- sealing: the seal control lives in the results state, which I
  cannot reach. Sprint 10's save was a no-JS server-action form I could POST to
  directly; that affordance is gone from the new page. I could not create a
  reading through the product.
  VERIFIED -- opening a sealed reading cold: the reading sealed during Sprint 10's
  test, 59fbb41d-82a4-4786-83eb-17924d654718, still resolves on a fresh
  request with no cookie jar: HTTP 200, zero Set-Cookie, rendered server-side:
  "Reading for 1969-07-20 | Sun Cancer 27.58 No | Moon Libra 3.50 No | Mercury
  Cancer 25.11 No | Venus Gemini 14.66 No | Mars Sagittarius 2.72 No | Jupiter
  Libra 0.70 No | Saturn Taurus 8.08 No | Uranus Libra 0.68 No | Neptune Scorpio
  26.02 Yes | Pluto Virgo 23.00 No". A freshly generated random id still 404s.
  So the retrieval half of the Sprint 10 guarantee demonstrably survived the UI
  replacement. The write half is unobserved.
  Note, not a defect: /reading/[id] still renders Sprint 10's plain table with no
  SVG. Nothing in this sprint's requirements asks for the reading page to adopt
  the constellation design -- R1 scopes the redesign to /chart's two states -- so
  this is in scope as built, not a miss. Flagging it only because someone
  comparing the two pages will notice the mismatch and should know it was not
  claimed.

CRITERION 4 -- a known historical date's positions still match a published source.
NOT TESTED.
  This needs the results state. I could not render positions for any date through
  the new UI.
  What I can say, and it is weaker than the criterion asks for: in Sprint 12,
  one commit earlier, /chart?date=2024-03-20 served positions byte-identical to
  the values I verified against NASA JPL Horizons in Sprint 6 (worst error 20.4
  arcsec across ten bodies). Sprint 13's R2 requires positions come from
  lib/ephemeris/ with no prototype ephemeris code, and QA1 passed that statically.
  But the criterion explicitly exists because "the design changed how the sky is
  drawn; it must not have changed what the sky was" -- and that is precisely the
  check I could not perform on this commit.

WHAT I COULD STILL VERIFY FROM SERVED ASSETS
  - R4, no runtime request to an external host: the served HTML references zero
    external hosts. No googleapis or gstatic font link of any kind. The shipped
    CSS contains no url() pointing off-origin.
    One thing I could NOT settle: the client JS chunks contain the string
    https://vercel.live, along with github.com and react.dev. Those last two are
    almost certainly React/Next error-message URLs rather than requests, and
    vercel.live is Vercel's own toolbar, which normally activates on preview
    deployments rather than production. I cannot confirm whether anything is
    actually requested at runtime without a browser's network panel. R4 is QA1's
    criterion, not mine, and QA1 passed it -- I raise this only so the one live
    check of R4 that matters, watching the network tab on production, is on
    someone's list rather than assumed from a grep.
  - R6, prefers-reduced-motion: the shipped stylesheet contains
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce). Present in the CSS actually served,
    not merely in the source. Whether it disables every ambient animation and
    leaves the chart legible is a visual judgement I cannot make without a browser.
  - Deployment observable intact: /api/health/db reports
    {"sha":"9b132e3abcd7ad8bb4e4b9407daaf05dac69b2af","short":"9b132e3",
     "isLocal":false}, matching Pipeman's ship and origin/main exactly.

WHAT THIS MEANS BEYOND THIS SPRINT -- the part worth acting on.
  I have caveated every report in this exercise with "no Playwright MCP or Chrome
  extension in this session". Until now that cost little: the product was
  server-rendered, so curl saw what a user saw. Sprint 13 changes that. The
  primary surface is now client-rendered, and a curl-only GroundTruth can no
  longer verify it -- not this sprint, and not any sprint after it that touches
  the chart UI.
  This is not a request for tooling as a convenience. It is the difference between
  a live gate that means something and one that reports on an empty state while
  the actual product goes unexamined. Attach Playwright MCP or Claude in Chrome to
  a GroundTruth session and criteria 1, 2, 3 and 4 are all straightforwardly
  testable: enter a date, watch the constellation render, scrub and watch it move,
  seal, and open the link in a clean context. That is one session's work, not a
  redesign.
  The alternative -- accepting a PASS on the strength of QA1's static audit plus a
  green empty state -- is exactly the "it passed QA1, so it's fine" reasoning this
  role exists to refuse.

WHAT WOULD CLEAR THIS TO A PASS
  A browser-equipped GroundTruth session re-testing criteria 1 (results state), 2
  (scrub), 3 (seal and open), and 4 (positions against JPL Horizons for a known
  date, as in Sprint 6). No code change is implied -- I found no defect. If a
  browser cannot be provided, the honest resolution is to amend the criteria to
  what can actually be verified and record why, as Sprint 5 did with previews,
  rather than to pass them unobserved.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks
are curl over HTTPS against production and direct inspection of served HTML, CSS
and JS assets. No JavaScript was executed, no rendering observed.
UX is being withdrawn ahead of a data-model revision.  It did not fail, but is being superseded
